body: The trust dialog belongs to the child's terminal: viola types no key into it and writes no byte to the terminal; when the write is skipped or lost the dialog is left whole to the human.
A started session that viola trusted must read to the human as an unwrapped start in an already trusted folder: no dialog, the CLI's own ready screen.

Verify's and the rig's reading of the child's screen stays signature-only: the first settled screen maps to a closed word from compiled signatures, no other screen content parsed, no screen text kept.
A skipped or failed trust write is no refusal: the run and revive starts add no stderr line, exit code or --json document for it and go on to the spawn.
The run log gains one closed word per start for the trust write's outcome; run diagnostics never reach the terminal and no path, key or value of the claude config reaches any line, stamp or summary.
Paths are not carried: the folder key and the config file's location appear in no printed output, log line or stamp.
Verify's trust-record write and removal stay silent on output: the outcome rides only the stamps' measured words, the verify step line unchanged.
Time bounds fall on the driver, never the human: the near-bound verify window case is bounded or its kill moved with measured walls, and every new waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s kill line.

Live readings never gate the build: the live re-read and the S1 and S2 starts run by hand under the founder's cap, each with a predicate its reading can fail, and the CI gate rests on the fake agent cases.
A change to the fake agent's trust reading or screens puts cli_verify in the gate block, and the fake agent's trust form stays the recorded one.
New verify and rig tests drive the outer PTY boundary only and assert on receipts and closed words, never on claude content.
The new --record case asserts the user's real claude config left untouched, or the chunk states why it cannot be asserted.
Tests reach both key rules: inside a repository the git root's key, outside any repository the cwd's key.

body_fields.convention: each new test runs inside the existing nextest suites and the coverage run; its failure is a nextest failure, with no skip and no separate a11y driver
each new test is deterministic: zero flakiness, no retries, a gate breach fails the build
each new boundary test is sequenced on records and receipts and never inspects claude content

The ledger stamps' measured field gains one closed word per interactive run's first settled screen (trust, imports, box, none), classified only from the existing compiled screen signatures. No screen text is kept anywhere.
Screen row text is read only by verify: the first-screen classification lives in verify. The run and revive start reads no screen content and types no key into the trust dialog.

A version is verified only when every relied row passes, and trust-record is a relied row. A live verify expects the floor of rows the live home's stamp names and reads red below it. pass and fail each have a named consequence: on fail with the floor held, the product write is not landed as relied.

The run and revive start order gains one step: after the version gate and before the child is spawned last, and only on a verified CLI, viola writes the per-project trust record when no record already trusts the folder. An unverified CLI keeps its transport-only degrade and gets no write.

The trust write is a widening of what viola writes outside its home: only projects[key].hasTrustDialogAccepted for one folder. No other key is changed, no entry removed, nothing is written for the home folder, and the file is never created.

The file the child reads is chosen from the claude_env_keep config key. viola reads CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR only when it is kept for the child and only for this purpose, and otherwise uses the user's own config file. This is a carve-out from the rule that CLAUDE names are stripped and that the environment is no configuration channel.

The config read is bounded and refused whole. If the file is absent, unreadable, a link, not a regular file, non-JSON or oversize, viola writes nothing and the dialog is left to the human. The file is parsed tolerantly as an external payload, and the CLI's own record shape is kept.

Each write takes the CLI's own lock file when it is free, replaces the file atomically through the atomic helper, reads the record back before the spawn, and makes at most 3 attempts. If the record is still lost, viola leaves the dialog to the human and types nothing. Losing another session's concurrent write in that window is an accepted, named residual.

The trust writer code words (written, key-present, lock-held, lost, config-absent, config-link, config-malformed, config-oversize, config-unreadable, config-not-regular, config-foreign, config-dir-unusable, home-unknown, removed) are the closed set the start logs. Each start logs one closed word to the run's codes-only role log, with nothing of the file's content.

The trust write's errors are typed in its own crate's error enum, and its messages interpolate nothing. viola-agent-claude does no file I/O, so the Claude record shape and key rule stay in that crate and the file I/O stays in the root bin.

The rig's seed is compared with what the writer writes, field by field and key by key: the path's spelling (canonical or not, a trailing separator, /tmp against its real path), every field beside hasTrustDialogAccepted, and the file's other top-level keys. Its finding feeds the writer and Run F.

The fake agent's trust reading and screens change. The fake agent reads its trust record the way the CLI does, so verify's runs and the start's trust write are proved in CI against it. A change to the fake agent's screens or trust reading puts cli_verify in the gate block.

The near-bound case verify_window_without_screens_fails_every_interactive_row (52.2 to 52.3 s against its 60 s kill) is bounded or has its kill moved, using the measured walls. Any waiting test stays under the 20 s root test-wait bound and lint.

A --record case asserts that the user's real claude config is left untouched. Verify's own trust record and the run's write must never reach a file outside the test's isolated home: each test runs in its own viola home and a private config dir.

Real claude CLI probes run only locally, never in CI. The live re-read and S1/S2 run on the standing rig under the founder's cap. Controls name --timeout S, ids are at most 16 characters, and no child screen is kept.

The two no-write rows saying viola writes nothing into the user's claude config are amended at this chunk's wrap, only if the write lands. Until then the per-project record is the only widening of viola's no-write rule.

The rule that the trust-record write and removal are uninstrumented meets the new run-log word: the chunk's start step must reconcile with that rule — one closed word per start and nothing more, no span fields, no detail-file record of the file.

Nothing of the user's claude config file reaches any line: no path to it, no project key, no folder path, no JSON content, in home-level lines, detail files, spans or stderr; detail codes carry no path or pid.

The one environment value viola reads to choose the target file (the kept CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) is never logged by value; environment is logged by names only and stripped or kept CLAUDE values never appear in telemetry.

verify's stamps gain a closed first-screen word per interactive run in measured (trust, imports, box, none) taken from the existing compiled signatures; no screen text is kept, no telemetry is derived from screen content, and verify's own log lines stay content-free.
The capability ledger's contents and stamps stay out of every log line; an unreadable ledger means an unverified CLI, and the write happens only on a verified CLI after the version gate.

The trust-record write is bounded at 3 attempts with a read-back before the spawn, against the plan's ban on retry policies and retry-once; the bounded attempt loop must be the named carve-out the scope gives, not a retry policy.

The run start span chain and its span attributes (run.version_gate, pty.spawn, run.start close): a new step between the version gate and the spawn, if spanned, takes a static name, skips all arguments and carries no path or env value.

Refusal cases (absent, unreadable, linked, non-JSON or oversize config file) write nothing and leave the dialog to the human; whether they surface as a parse-rejected line or only as the closed run-log word, the detail word is closed and pathless.
Real-CLI verify never runs in CI and CI verify runs against the fake agent only; the fake agent's changed trust reading and screens put cli_verify in the gate block.
The near-bound verify window case: verify's interactive rows killed at the verify_window_ bound, read with the measured walls; a waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint and waits on no sleep.

A live verify reads the floor of rows the live home's stamp names and is RED below it; trust-record pass and fail each carry a named consequence, and verify's summary and stop lines report it without content.

The e2e rig's V arm prints the first-screen words before teardown and keeps no child screen; test homes and scratch roots stay under the scanned e2e root and the user's real claude config is asserted untouched.
The child process-start line of the claude child keeps its env fields (env_kept, env_stripped_count) unchanged by the target-file choice; the diagnostics line schema stays additive only.

Verify itself still never answers or types into a dialog: the first-screen word is a reading only, and a trust or imports screen ends the run as a reading, never with a key.

The live rig's V arm: a git-initialised scratch root with the record seeded at the root's key, Runs B to E inside it, Run F in a fresh directory outside any repository; the rig child stays isolated from the user's own config, keys only into its own pty, and its first-screen words are printed before teardown as closed words.

The product write itself: at run and revive, after the version gate and before the spawn, on a verified CLI only (the unverified CLI gate holds), when no record already trusts the folder, viola writes only projects[key].hasTrustDialogAccepted for one folder — no other key changed, no entry removed, nothing written for the home folder.
The trust record key: the key the CLI itself writes on an accepted dialog — the git root inside a repository, else the cwd.

The target file: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR's .claude.json when viola's home keeps that variable for the child through claude_env_keep, else the user's own .claude.json; viola reads that one environment value for that one purpose — a new environment read that needs its log entry, and its value never logged.

The writer's guards: an absent, unreadable, symlinked, non-JSON or oversize file means viola writes nothing and never creates it, and the dialog is the human's; the read of the file is bounded; a refusal never blocks the human.

The write's concurrency: take the CLI's own lock when free, replace the file atomically through the one shared replace helper, read the record back before the spawn, at most 3 attempts; a record still lost leaves the dialog to the human and viola types nothing; the residual of a concurrent write lost in the window is accepted by the founder's word and named in the row.

The boundary widening: viola now writes the per-project trust record into the Claude config — named as a widening, with its security-plan Decisions Log entry; the two rows saying viola writes nothing into the Claude config or under the Claude home are amended at this chunk's wrap, only if the write lands.

The trust record writer guarded and its outcomes as closed code words: one closed word per start in the run log, nothing of the file's content or path anywhere — in the log, the error output or diagnostics.
The stamps file: written only by verify, checked under lock and through the strict-modes check before it is read by the version gate; the new measured words are a change to the stamps' format.
What a user's existing home reads once the row is relied by run: a stamp without the trust-record row is transport-only until its next live verify, and the product write stays off on it.
The near-bound case: the verify-window test reads 52.2 to 52.3 s against its 60 s kill — bound the case or move its kill, with the measured walls; a waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint.
The named gap: a record case asserting the user's real Claude config file untouched by verify, or a stated reason it cannot be.

body: Verify classifies each interactive run's first settled screen into one closed word (trust, imports, box, none) from the existing compiled screen signatures only; no screen text is kept anywhere, no assertion reads the rendered child screen.
The stamps' format gains the measured first-screen words; stamps stay written only by verify, verify the single stamp writer, and a stamp refuses a widened ledger.

The trust-record ledger row's live re-read: a live verify expects the floor of rows the live home's stamp names and reads red below it; trust-record pass and fail each carry a named consequence, and on fail the product write is not landed as relied. A live reading is recorded as read, never as verification, and a fake-agent run is no proof of the real CLI.

The version gate needs every relied ledger row; the trust write happens only on a verified CLI, after the version gate and before the child spawn, at both viola run and viola revive, keeping the run checks-before-spawn order and the revive preflight order.

The writer writes only projects[key].hasTrustDialogAccepted for one folder, key the git root inside a repository else the cwd; no other key changed, no entry removed, nothing written for the home folder, nothing written when a record already trusts the folder.

The file written is the one the started child reads: the config dir's file when viola's home keeps CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for the child through claude_env_keep, else the user's own; viola reads that one env value for that one purpose, against the CLAUDE* environment strip of the child.

An absent, unreadable, linked, non-JSON or oversize config file makes viola write nothing and never create it, the dialog left to the human; the read is bounded, JSON depth bounded, and the file's contents never reach an error body, a log or a diagnostic.

The write takes the CLI's own lock when free, replaces atomically, reads the record back before the spawn, at most 3 attempts; a record still lost leaves the trust dialog to the human and viola types no key — no blanket dialog approval.
One closed word per start in the run log for the trust write outcome, a new closed set of words that changes only by decision, with no path or file content in the log or in errors.

The live rig's V arm git-initialises its scratch root and seeds the record at the root's key so Runs B to E read the git-root key, Run F stays in a fresh dir outside any repository; the rig prints the first-screen words before teardown; the rig is local-only, never in CI.

Before any live start, the rig's seeded trust entry is compared field by field and key by key with the writer's record (path spelling, trailing separator, temp dir against its real path, every field beside the accepted flag, the file's other top-level keys), from the code alone.

The live proof S1 and its control S2 run under the founder's cap: controls name and fire with a --timeout, ids at most 16 characters, every live start counted per CLI version with every byte typed named.

The near-bound case verify_window_without_screens_fails_every_interactive_row reads 52.2 to 52.3 s against its 60 s verify_window_ kill: bound the case or move its kill, with the measured walls, keeping kill lines below the mutants timeout.

A recording verify case asserts the user's real claude config untouched, or the chunk says why it cannot; test verifies run under a test-owned user home and never read the host's claude sessions or config.

The writer's tests run on real files in a fresh test-made home, the config file seeded by the test itself, filesystem faults (link, unreadable, oversize, non-JSON, held lock) made real, never mocked.
Every waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s kill line for stamped-home and verify-driven tests, and every root wait stays bounded below its kill.
